finding: Byte-level PDF mutations are not tracked as unsaved edits.
evidence: src/store.tsx:717-722 checks only annotations, formValues, and fieldOps, while text, object, page, OCR, and redaction operations replace document bytes.
impact: Users can close or refresh without a warning and lose edits, including applied redactions.
fix: Track an explicit saved revision or content hash and mark every mutating path dirty.

finding: Standard encrypted PDFs can become unreadable when processed by helper paths.
evidence: src/lib/pdftools.ts:48 loads through pdf-lib with ignoreEncryption:true; src/lib/pdfium.ts:53 reopens with an empty password; a diagnostic output could not be reopened by PDFium with either the user password or no password.
impact: Protected customer documents can be corrupted or silently lose protection.
fix: Use the authenticated PDFium handle or an explicit owner-decrypt, mutate, validate, and re-encrypt pipeline.

finding: The 270-degree viewer-to-PDF coordinate transform is wrong.
evidence: src/lib/pdftools.ts:460-475 and 1804-1818 swap width and height incorrectly; a 600x800 diagnostic produced x=540,y=450 instead of PDFium's x=340,y=650.
impact: Crop, redaction, annotations, OCR, and form placement can affect the wrong region on rotated pages.
fix: Replace hand-coded branches with one PDFium-backed transform and rotation fixtures.

finding: Redaction can silently fail while the UI removes boxes and reports success.
evidence: src/lib/pdfium.ts:200-226 skips failed pages and ignores a false redaction result; src/store.tsx:2213-2229 removes boxes and shows success without post-save verification.
impact: Sensitive content may remain recoverable after a user is told it was permanently removed.
fix: Fail closed on every page/quad error and reopen, extract, inspect objects, and render the output before success.

finding: Image-only redactions do not remove the underlying image despite unconditional removal claims.
evidence: TODO.md:83-88 records that image-only regions are only covered; the UI and marketing claim text and images are deleted and nothing is recoverable.
impact: The privacy promise is unsafe for scanned PDFs, a primary redaction use case.
fix: Implement destructive image/path redaction or detect and block unsupported regions with precise messaging.

finding: Page copy operations discard document-level structures.
evidence: src/lib/pdftools.ts:52-130 rebuilds documents using copyPages; diagnostics changed test-form.pdf from four fields to zero and removed the outline from test-outline.pdf.
impact: Merge, extract, delete, and reorder can destroy forms, outlines, destinations, tags, attachments, signatures, and catalog settings.
fix: Mutate the page tree in place or explicitly preserve and remap every catalog structure, with round-trip fixtures.

finding: Permanent crop changes page boxes but leaves hidden content recoverable.
evidence: src/lib/pdftools.ts:237-257 only sets CropBox and MediaBox while src/components/tools/ToolsScreens.tsx:1105-1114 says the cropped area is removed permanently.
impact: Users may disclose supposedly removed content.
fix: Rename it boundary crop or truly rewrite/clamp page content and verify removal.

finding: PDF permission enforcement is incomplete and spread across UI paths.
evidence: Split/extract, export, search/replace, and OCR paths lack centralized copy, assembly, or modify checks.
impact: Restricted PDFs can be modified or exported through alternate workflows.
fix: Enforce authorization inside every store mutation/export API rather than only in controls.

finding: Whole-PDF undo history is memory-unbounded by bytes and leaks discarded PDFium proxies.
evidence: src/store.tsx:780 retains up to 60 full byte arrays/proxies and discarded history entries are sliced without destroying their proxies.
impact: Large PDFs can exhaust memory or crash long sessions.
fix: Use a byte-budgeted history, destroy every discarded proxy, and store deltas or temporary files.

finding: Rendering is synchronous, non-cancellable, and lacks resource limits.
evidence: src/lib/engine.ts:449 has a no-op cancel path; rendering copies full RGBA buffers and viewer startup caches every page handle.
impact: Large or malicious documents can freeze or exhaust the UI process.
fix: Move rendering/extraction to workers, tile pages, add real cancellation, and enforce pixel/page/file budgets.

finding: The desktop and live web surfaces lack a defensive content security policy and security headers.
evidence: src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:28 sets csp:null; the live marketing audit scored 25/100 with HSTS, CSP, frame, MIME, referrer, and permissions headers absent.
impact: Injection, clickjacking, downgrade, and secret-exposure risks are harder to contain.
fix: Ship a restrictive CSP and the six baseline response headers on both origins.
source: source audit and live header check

finding: Untrusted link schemes and arbitrary AI endpoints are accepted, while API keys are stored in localStorage.
evidence: PDF and user links lack a strict scheme allow-list; custom endpoints accept arbitrary URLs; src/store.tsx:1113 serializes settings including customApiKey.
impact: A malicious PDF or injection could expose secrets or launch unsafe protocols.
fix: Allow-list schemes, confirm external launches, require HTTPS except loopback, and use an OS credential vault on desktop.

finding: Local document, signature, chat, and API-key retention is not visible or controllable enough.
evidence: IndexedDB retains up to ten 80 MB documents, closed files are not deleted, signatures and the last 40 chat messages persist, and failures are silent.
impact: Local-first does not equal ephemeral; regulated users need retention and deletion control.
fix: Add no-retention mode, per-item and clear-all deletion, retention disclosure, and protected secret storage.

finding: The editor is not keyboard or assistive-technology ready.
evidence: Custom dialogs lack dialog semantics/focus trapping, form inputs lack programmatic labels, object overlays are pointer-only, the text editor is an unlabeled contenteditable, and multiple controls are below 44 pixels.
impact: The product is unusable for some users and cannot meet enterprise/public-sector accessibility requirements.
fix: Adopt accessible dialog primitives, labels, keyboard object editing, axe tests, and PDF tagging/remediation workflows.

finding: Critical PDF workflows have no integration, interoperability, corpus, fuzz, or end-to-end coverage.
evidence: 79 unit tests in eight files pass, but Rust has zero tests and no CI, E2E, coverage, visual regression, corpus, fuzz, or accessibility suite exists.
impact: Release-blocking encryption, rotation, redaction, and structure-loss defects reached the current build.
fix: Create a golden PDF corpus and invariant-based CI across open, edit, save, reopen, render, extract, and validate.

finding: The public Download and GitHub links return 404 and no public release is available.
evidence: Live broken-link checks returned 404 for github.com/naumanahmed19/pdfeditor and its releases path; the local remote is private/unavailable anonymously and there are no tags.
impact: Visitors cannot install or verify the product, so acquisition and conversion stop at the CTA.
fix: Publish a real release destination with checksums, release notes, and supported installers before advertising download.

finding: Available installer artifacts are unsigned, test-signed, or fail trust validation.
evidence: Get-AuthenticodeSignature reported unsigned PDF Workbench builds, UnknownError with CN=PickPDF Test Code Signing for 0.1.0, and an unsigned PickPDF 0.1.1 setup.
impact: Windows trust warnings and SmartScreen friction undermine a privacy/security product.
fix: Use a production code-signing identity, timestamp every artifact, and automate verified release signing.

finding: Public claims overstate implemented behavior and commercial readiness.
evidence: The site claims lossless compression, complete redaction, very-large-file performance, automatic updates, signed installers, central seat management, deployment, and DPA support while source/live legal pages show lossy JPEG recompression, image redaction gaps, no updater/admin stack, test signing, and planned DPA/commerce.
impact: Trust, legal, refund, and enterprise procurement risk outweigh short-term conversion gains.
fix: Publish only verified capabilities and label Pro/Team as preview until purchase, licensing, support, and legal delivery exist.
source: source, artifact, and live copy audit

finding: Three guide URLs in the sitemap canonicalize to the guides hub.
evidence: All three guide routes return 200 but declare https://pickpdf.app/guides as canonical.
impact: Search engines are instructed to consolidate the guide pages instead of indexing them.
fix: Give each finished guide a self-referencing canonical or remove it from the sitemap.

finding: The browser editor origin returns the same indexable SPA shell with HTTP 200 for robots, sitemap, and nonexistent paths.
evidence: open.pickpdf.app/robots.txt and a random nonexistent URL both returned the 730-byte PickPDF shell with HTTP 200; the shell has no noindex, canonical, or description.
impact: The origin creates soft-404/crawl-noise risk and weak duplicate brand pages.
fix: Return real 404s and apply X-Robots-Tag:noindex,nofollow to the app shell.

finding: Thirteen commercial routes have no inbound HTML links.
evidence: All eight tool pages, four comparison pages, and /guides were discoverable only through the sitemap.
impact: Crawl priority, authority flow, usability, and conversions are weak.
fix: Create a tools hub, make homepage tiles real links, and cross-link related tools, guides, and comparisons.

finding: Commercial and guide pages are too thin and generic to compete.
evidence: Tool pages contain roughly 135-165 rendered words, comparisons 108-121, guides 103-111, and teams 132 including shared navigation/footer.
impact: Pages do not demonstrate expertise, satisfy intent, or earn citations against established competitors.
fix: Add task-specific product interaction, evidence, screenshots, limitations, examples, related links, authorship, and 600-1000+ useful words where needed.

finding: Metadata is systematically outside useful search-snippet ranges.
evidence: Twenty-two descriptions are under 120 characters, the homepage description is 180, six titles are under 30, and the pricing title is 67.
impact: Relevance signals and organic click-through potential are weaker, though length alone is not a ranking penalty.
fix: Write unique query-matched titles, descriptions, and H1s for all sitemap routes.

finding: The site lacks the trust and authority layer needed for privacy and regulated-workflow claims.
evidence: No About page, named team, author bios, security contact, company identity, benchmarks, case studies, public changelog, independent reviews, or substantive DPA exists.
impact: Users, search engines, and enterprise buyers cannot validate who operates the product or its claims.
fix: Publish About, Contact, Security, privacy architecture, changelog, named authors, reproducible benchmarks, and independent assessment.

finding: AI-search readiness is incomplete.
evidence: llms.txt returns 404, AI crawler policy is implicit, and only the homepage contains JSON-LD.
impact: The brand is harder to cite and understand in answer engines.
fix: Add llms.txt, explicit crawler policy, Organization/WebSite schema, TechArticle schema, authors, and quotable benchmark data.

finding: The production editor payload and local AI default create substantial first-use cost.
evidence: Build output contains a 2.19 MB main JS chunk, 4.63 MB PDFium WASM, 23.57 MB ONNX runtime WASM, and a default Gemma model documented at about 3 GB and 8 GB RAM.
impact: Cold start, low-end devices, mobile usability, and completion rates suffer.
fix: Code-split by workflow, lazy-load engines, use workers, ship a smaller default model, and measure p75 first-page and interaction latency.

finding: Professional PDF parity features are absent or partial.
evidence: No PKI signature validation, accessibility remediation/PDF-UA, PDF/A/X/E/VT validation, preflight/print production, autosave/versioning, full-fidelity conversions, multi-language OCR/deskew, collaboration/e-sign routing, API/SDK, or enterprise administration exists.
impact: The product cannot yet replace Acrobat, Foxit, Nitro, Smallpdf, or iLovePDF for their strongest buyer segments.
fix: Win the private local-first editing wedge first, then build professional and enterprise parity in measured stages.

finding: The deployed marketing application is not owned by the tracked checkout.
evidence: The live sitemap exposes 23 routes, but this repository only special-cases /download and .gitignore excludes landing/; the deployed router, sitemap generator, and route source are absent.
impact: SEO, legal copy, and release changes cannot be reviewed or gated with the product source.
fix: Bring deployment source and infrastructure into version control with preview deployments and crawl/security CI.

finding: The current checkout typechecks, builds, and passes its existing unit and dependency checks.
evidence: TypeScript passed; Vitest passed 79/79; npm audit found zero advisories; Cargo compiled and cargo test completed with zero Rust tests.
impact: The codebase has a useful baseline but the checks do not exercise release-critical PDF invariants.
fix: Keep these gates and add corpus, E2E, security, performance, and accessibility validation.
